title: Last Menstrual Period
subject: Obstetrics & gynaecology
summary: The date of the last menstrual period (LMP) is the cornerstone for estimating gestational age when cycles are regular. Accurate LMP dating guides antenatal care, screening, and timing of interventions, especially in low‑resource settings where ultrasound may be limited.

sections.p: LMP is the first day of the most recent normal menstrual bleeding. It is used to calculate gestational age (GA) by adding 280 days (40 weeks).
b: Requires a regular 28‑±7‑day cycle and reliable recall
If cycle is irregular, use ultrasound or fundal height as adjunct

sections.p: LMP itself is not a disease, but inaccurate dating can lead to mis‑staging of pregnancy complications (e.g., pre‑eclampsia, preterm labour).
b: Early pregnancy (<12 weeks) – dating critical for viability decisions
Mid‑trimester (13‑27 weeks) – informs anomaly scan timing
Late pregnancy (≥28 weeks) – guides induction and delivery planning
Irregular cycles (PCOS, thyroid disease, malnutrition)
Recent hormonal contraception or emergency contraception
Bleeding disorders or uterine pathology causing spotting
Recall bias – common in low‑literacy settings

sections.p: Patients may present with uncertainty about dates, especially adolescents, refugees, or women with low health literacy.
b: Unclear first day of bleed
Variable flow or intermenstrual spotting
Recent use of hormonal methods

sections.p: When LMP is uncertain, supplement with bedside tools.

t.b: Estimates GA when ultrasound unavailable; discrepancy >2 cm suggests dating error
Confirms GA by crown‑rump length (first trimester) or biparietal diameter (second trimester)
Confirms pregnancy when LMP unknown; positive indicates need for dating work‑up
Standardised questions to improve recall; if unavailable, use community health worker interview

sections.p: Incorrect dating can mask or delay recognition of serious obstetric conditions.
b: Severe abdominal pain with uncertain GA – consider ectopic pregnancy
Bleeding after 20 weeks with unknown LMP – assess for placenta previa or abruption
Hypertension before 20 weeks – may indicate molar pregnancy

sections.p: Goal: obtain the most accurate GA possible and document uncertainty.
b: Ask structured menstrual history (first day, cycle length, regularity)
If LMP unreliable, use fundal height and, when possible, ultrasound
Document confidence level (e.g., ‘LMP reliable’, ‘LMP uncertain – GA based on fundal height’)
Avoid invasive procedures (e.g., amniocentesis) until GA is reasonably certain

sections.p: Educate women on tracking cycles to improve future dating.
b: Provide simple calendar or mobile reminder tools
Counsel on regular antenatal visits for repeat dating checks
Integrate menstrual education into community health outreach
Expected date of delivery (EDD) – calculated from LMP but not the same
Menstrual irregularities due to endocrine disease – affect dating reliability
Assuming regular 28‑day cycles in women with PCOS – leads to over‑estimation of GA
Relying on patient‑reported LMP without confirming with physical exam in late presentation

whenToSeekHelp: Severe abdominal pain with unknown LMP – possible ectopic pregnancy
Heavy vaginal bleeding after 20 weeks with uncertain dating – possible placenta previa or abruption
Sudden hypertension before 20 weeks – consider molar pregnancy

faq.q: What if the patient cannot recall her LMP?
faq.a: Use fundal height, ultrasound if available, and a detailed menstrual questionnaire; document the uncertainty.

faq.q: How accurate is fundal height for dating?
faq.a: Within ±2 cm of expected measurement for a given GA; useful when ultrasound is not accessible.

faq.q: Can hormonal contraception affect LMP dating?
faq.a: Yes; recent use can cause delayed or absent periods, making LMP unreliable.

exam: A 22‑year‑old presents at 10 weeks gestation but cannot recall her LMP – what is your next step? — Obtain a focused menstrual history, measure fundal height, and arrange a dating ultrasound if possible.
How does an irregular 35‑day cycle affect GA calculation from LMP? — It introduces ±7‑day uncertainty; use ultrasound or fundal height to refine dating.
Why is accurate LMP essential before initiating antenatal steroids? — Steroids are given before 34 weeks; mis‑dating could expose a term fetus to unnecessary medication.
A woman with known PCOS reports her LMP 8 weeks ago; fundal height suggests 12 weeks. How do you reconcile? — Recognise LMP likely inaccurate; rely on fundal height/ultrasound for GA.
What red‑flag symptom in a woman with unknown LMP warrants immediate ultrasound? — Severe unilateral abdominal pain or shoulder tip pain suggesting ectopic pregnancy.

Explain how you would counsel a rural patient on tracking her cycles for future pregnancies. — Provide a simple paper calendar, teach the importance of noting the first day of bleed, and encourage regular antenatal visits.
During a labour ward audit, many records list EDD but not LMP. Why is this problematic? — Without LMP the confidence in GA is reduced; EDD alone may hide dating errors affecting management decisions.
A patient on hormonal IUD presents with a 6‑week pregnancy; how reliable is her LMP? — Not reliable; IUD can cause irregular bleeding; dating should rely on ultrasound.
